item.title: Trump, Xi and Putin Set for Rare APEC Trilateral Talks
item.description:
Nov 16th, 2026
Trump, Xi and Putin Set for Rare APEC Trilateral Talks
US President Donald Trump, Chinese President Xi Jinping and Russian President Vladimir Putin are set to hold a rare trilateral meeting Thursday on the sidelines of the APEC summit in Shenzhen. Reporting from Shenzhen, Bloomberg’s Stephen Engle says that while the White House is framing the talks around denuclearization, the conflicts in Ukraine and Iran are likely to come up in discussions.

US equity-index futures rose in early Asian trading, pointing to a tentative recovery in market sentiment after a bout of weakness late last week. Oil slipped.
Contracts for the Nasdaq 100 rose 0.5%, while S&P 500 futures gained 0.2% after both underlying benchmarks capped a second straight day of losses on Friday. MSCI Inc.’s gauge of Asian shares inched lower. Global benchmark Brent crude traded around $95.50 a barrel after a two-week slump, as fresh attacks in the Middle East countered signs of a well-supplied physical market.

Goldman Sachs Group Inc. and Morgan Stanley are taking opposing views on the yen, highlighting the increasing difficulty in forecasting a currency being pulled in different directions.
Morgan Stanley strategists including Serena Tang see the yen weakening to 162 per dollar by the fourth quarter of 2027, arguing that strong global risk appetite, Japan’s terms of trade and the continued appeal of carry trades will ultimately outweigh support from narrowing interest-rate differentials.

Takeaways by Bloomberg AI
Indonesian authorities may struggle to put a floor under Asia’s worst-performing currency, according to strategists, as rising domestic political uncertainty and further capital outflows weigh on the rupiah.
BNP Paribas SA expects the rupiah to plummet to 18,500 per dollar by the end of next year, while MUFG Bank Ltd. sees it weakening to 18,350 this quarter. Mizuho Bank Ltd. also expects further downside for the Indonesian currency, which dropped to an all-time low against the dollar last week.

Takeaways by Bloomberg AI
Australia’s resources minister has expressed concern that state-backed buyer China Mineral Resources Group Co.’s negotiations with iron ore suppliers could breach international trade rules.
Beijing set up CMRG four years ago to strengthen the purchasing power of its enormous steel sector after bristling at the hefty profits being raked up by the Australian and Brazilian iron ore miners it depended on. There is now growing unease about its market influence. China accounts for more than 70% of global seaborne iron ore demand and more than half of global steel production.

Takeaways by Bloomberg AI
Bitcoin’s latest selloff is testing the resolve of some of the cryptocurrency market’s most committed investors, as a succession of setbacks pushes prices toward their lowest levels of the year and major sources of demand weaken.
The largest digital asset slumped toward $62,000 in weekend trading, reaching its weakest level since July, before stabilizing at around $65,000 by Monday morning in Asia. Its drop of more than 20% over the past month has gathered pace in recent weeks. Unlike the abrupt crashes that have punctuated previous crypto downturns, much of the preceding decline unfolded during relatively subdued trading before liquidations accelerated in recent days.

Takeaways by Bloomberg AI
Vietnam’s retail investors are dumping equities and buying high-yielding notes from banks to capture interest rates nearing 10%, as locals and foreigners fall out of favor with the poor-performing stock market.
Banks lifted deposit rates in recent months to compete for funding, sucking in a swathe of the country’s 14 million retail investors to a financial product long considered out of fashion. The move came as the roughly $392 billion equity market dropped about 3% in 2026, on course for its first annual loss in four years.
